[Highlight start] **Advil (ibuprofen) is generally preferred over Tylenol (acetaminophen) for a hangover** [Highlight end] because combining alcohol with Tylenol increases the risk of liver damage. However, both medications carry risks after drinking, so neither is completely risk-free.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF15A2USzW9jJehnJOUR1XricrSUg52n_ZD843udUjGYxbBzC9wjB4Rua3loQ-Qq4Nj11zCvOvaO-ifMNsI58eurV8j_jpE8IeULgBS-_vevMcgpvvZii7E1CnLikoqeoPl6lKOWy_BQq1T1P-EUgXqb2wuGjvS7pG7c3sgWFNQZgij4U7Xxb5Az7EQR50taQE)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkQEBxCJF18RRjW0gmwFOHOtiqa7eSTfsQLn8yu1ilkXHsKHBYdFBG78eLzJAvwqXELYPljulUCwFvoJWRaQeEFoZiTlYWMhY8jVKBK70oziV7TXSTO4mfl7DsntkaTc_HohGbsNKwv06R3Mw2wAiiOWz65j4VrJOlA3_nMzwei8Rh5vE0u1K9dYgbbVnXTL4C4FX)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXXwOQLCjUYVRaCeFQUHKybfE7b30uz4NofEQxbzriHd08y4pMz6ADyc8GwTOsbDK3uXjJMtkben3-eL1N1g1uU1BH2GzV561-TvneyrNWIqRMQuYUmj3fYHY_4zHu8RdJ22ZMu8RKCJrcm_KaqRQ)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF18AGg2HYY2MASNfn8JZ7nN7s5-LWZVVeXTxrw--R05xrgAo90oHltcbpGUbhE9wvn2iu1FzK94FJl741l-9rfRiuu_NNf0K1Ivdnuf9F7HUWneHPN1IqRnyuPe2tamwnqU0B4SHCT3mWzdeYBE1SkwKZU1Gmw6odkuC33g)

### Advil (Ibuprofen)

- **Pros:** Targets inflammation and helps ease hangover headaches and body aches without adding strain to the liver.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkQEBxCJF18RRjW0gmwFOHOtiqa7eSTfsQLn8yu1ilkXHsKHBYdFBG78eLzJAvwqXELYPljulUCwFvoJWRaQeEFoZiTlYWMhY8jVKBK70oziV7TXSTO4mfl7DsntkaTc_HohGbsNKwv06R3Mw2wAiiOWz65j4VrJOlA3_nMzwei8Rh5vE0u1K9dYgbbVnXTL4C4FX)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXXwOQLCjUYVRaCeFQUHKybfE7b30uz4NofEQxbzriHd08y4pMz6ADyc8GwTOsbDK3uXjJMtkben3-eL1N1g1uU1BH2GzV561-TvneyrNWIqRMQuYUmj3fYHY_4zHu8RdJ22ZMu8RKCJrcm_KaqRQ)
- **Cons & Risks:** Can irritate your stomach lining—especially when alcohol has already irritated it—and may affect the kidneys or cause stomach bleeding in some people.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXW24s3PzIPtRkF1Dj0SD2PLoUsqa6-f_0D91z3ca-SnZJcvPQTf_Wimm_DXfjoRR-zs9qz3WA_qRaL3WR1J0d4_FPmwL3AopDsAFkl3wP8QUVAomPcm8nXqHw-IfGPj1gGr4Q8B8t2mkfxcYxd6ha)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkQEBxCJF18RRjW0gmwFOHOtiqa7eSTfsQLn8yu1ilkXHsKHBYdFBG78eLzJAvwqXELYPljulUCwFvoJWRaQeEFoZiTlYWMhY8jVKBK70oziV7TXSTO4mfl7DsntkaTc_HohGbsNKwv06R3Mw2wAiiOWz65j4VrJOlA3_nMzwei8Rh5vE0u1K9dYgbbVnXTL4C4FX)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXLMH0LQ6jy88GEl8ahjHG-RI_ZOMwZPPuWHyUzHsHR-LGXLq0KiaslIcPw1V_Yihn9hPcBF8o9OiSo5rUS_QOyld-GhyC6vCEllCLr3xIkWNV3oq3oNbjUGjNAQKL550-Gw)
- **How to use more safely:** Take it with food and plenty of water after you stop drinking, and avoid it if you have stomach ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, or kidney issues.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF18AGg2HYY2MASNfn8JZ7nN7s5-LWZVVeXTxrw--R05xrgAo90oHltcbpGUbhE9wvn2iu1FzK94FJl741l-9rfRiuu_NNf0K1Ivdnuf9F7HUWneHPN1IqRnyuPe2tamwnqU0B4SHCT3mWzdeYBE1SkwKZU1Gmw6odkuC33g)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXW24s3PzIPtRkF1Dj0SD2PLoUsqa6-f_0D91z3ca-SnZJcvPQTf_Wimm_DXfjoRR-zs9qz3WA_qRaL3WR1J0d4_FPmwL3AopDsAFkl3wP8QUVAomPcm8nXqHw-IfGPj1gGr4Q8B8t2mkfxcYxd6ha)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXXwOQLCjUYVRaCeFQUHKybfE7b30uz4NofEQxbzriHd08y4pMz6ADyc8GwTOsbDK3uXjJMtkben3-eL1N1g1uU1BH2GzV561-TvneyrNWIqRMQuYUmj3fYHY_4zHu8RdJ22ZMu8RKCJrcm_KaqRQ)

### Tylenol (Acetaminophen)

- **Pros:** Does not cause the same direct stomach lining irritation as NSAIDs like ibuprofen.
- **Cons & Risks:** Mixing alcohol with acetaminophen can cause serious liver toxicity, as both are processed through the liver. Medical guidance from sources like [Mayo Clinic](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF15A2USzW9jJehnJOUR1XricrSUg52n_ZD843udUjGYxbBzC9wjB4Rua3loQ-Qq4Nj11zCvOvaO-ifMNsI58eurV8j_jpE8IeULgBS-_vevMcgpvvZii7E1CnLikoqeoPl6lKOWy_BQq1T1P-EUgXqb2wuGjvS7pG7c3sgWFNQZgij4U7Xxb5Az7EQR50taQE) and [Harvard Health](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkQEBxCJF18RRjW0gmwFOHOtiqa7eSTfsQLn8yu1ilkXHsKHBYdFBG78eLzJAvwqXELYPljulUCwFvoJWRaQeEFoZiTlYWMhY8jVKBK70oziV7TXSTO4mfl7DsntkaTc_HohGbsNKwv06R3Mw2wAiiOWz65j4VrJOlA3_nMzwei8Rh5vE0u1K9dYgbbVnXTL4C4FX) warns against taking Tylenol when alcohol is in your system.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF15A2USzW9jJehnJOUR1XricrSUg52n_ZD843udUjGYxbBzC9wjB4Rua3loQ-Qq4Nj11zCvOvaO-ifMNsI58eurV8j_jpE8IeULgBS-_vevMcgpvvZii7E1CnLikoqeoPl6lKOWy_BQq1T1P-EUgXqb2wuGjvS7pG7c3sgWFNQZgij4U7Xxb5Az7EQR50taQE)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkQEBxCJF18RRjW0gmwFOHOtiqa7eSTfsQLn8yu1ilkXHsKHBYdFBG78eLzJAvwqXELYPljulUCwFvoJWRaQeEFoZiTlYWMhY8jVKBK70oziV7TXSTO4mfl7DsntkaTc_HohGbsNKwv06R3Mw2wAiiOWz65j4VrJOlA3_nMzwei8Rh5vE0u1K9dYgbbVnXTL4C4FX)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXPzREAO2W0uKCeEBUKEVcTBfCFmS1p3Ryv1oDXGMc2Q1f2P3z5VEjF-HdzSN_V3T_yhzY6B4p4pVEB1KfRe4b5xo0lOj2J54-JMxImIPVmylX41sXRWuNo31NF_fctZHM)

For broader hangover care, sipping water or electrolyte fluids, eating bland foods, and resting help support recovery while your body clears the alcohol. (If you have liver or kidney conditions, stomach issues, or take daily medications like blood thinners, check with a doctor or pharmacist before taking either.)[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF15A2USzW9jJehnJOUR1XricrSUg52n_ZD843udUjGYxbBzC9wjB4Rua3loQ-Qq4Nj11zCvOvaO-ifMNsI58eurV8j_jpE8IeULgBS-_vevMcgpvvZii7E1CnLikoqeoPl6lKOWy_BQq1T1P-EUgXqb2wuGjvS7pG7c3sgWFNQZgij4U7Xxb5Az7EQR50taQE)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESywEBxCJF181Cbd9lhKHT5A_d2KMZWTSn1zNEudWupiAUCtxtmuuHNrjEuS5z3k-AcPIAVYyW59M3RG4GRjwxDsydpqNoZlJhmZf0gIIUhbSE9wSqRSfvTGC0qnDON3fXyCHNITVzA0wcgxI23qVnKHiyaZp96cos3B4_i4MGYV0NRisXqf8eRWjRBLnDqJkQJAYNZknvb32QfFFF9Bsn3GP-mFjICGtBnDidagXuLK6jKzyPDekvuYyFIpW0ZJkwVwj7RI8RFJQQkegkGw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF18AGg2HYY2MASNfn8JZ7nN7s5-LWZVVeXTxrw--R05xrgAo90oHltcbpGUbhE9wvn2iu1FzK94FJl741l-9rfRiuu_NNf0K1Ivdnuf9F7HUWneHPN1IqRnyuPe2tamwnqU0B4SHCT3mWzdeYBE1SkwKZU1Gmw6odkuC33g)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXLMH0LQ6jy88GEl8ahjHG-RI_ZOMwZPPuWHyUzHsHR-LGXLq0KiaslIcPw1V_Yihn9hPcBF8o9OiSo5rUS_QOyld-GhyC6vCEllCLr3xIkWNV3oq3oNbjUGjNAQKL550-Gw)If you'd like to narrow this down, let me know:
